extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal foundation models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It comprises 11.5K multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six core disciplines and 30 subjects, spanning 183 subfields and 30 heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection took three stages: first, selecting university majors/subjects where visual inputs provide valuable information (ruling out subjects like law and linguistics); second, recruiting over 50 university students (including coauthors) specializing in these majors as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, quizzes, and free online resources, or creating new questions based on expertise where necessary. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to reduce contamination risks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Major textbooks, quizzes, online resources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed: first, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to detect potential duplicate problems, followed by author review to eliminate duplicates; second, problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. In a third stage, problems were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions, answer options, correct answers, image types, difficulty ratings, and optional explanations were annotated into a structured JSON format following specific guidelines. All questions were required to have one or more images, be in English, meet college-level difficulty, and be clearly categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality, and regular audits of random samples were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicate problems were reviewed and eliminated by authors. Format and typo checking were conducted across co-authors. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for detailed review and examined collaboratively in team meetings to establish a standardized approach.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college/university students (including co-authors) specializing in the 30 corresponding majors/disciplines; 90 college senior students (3 per subject) served as subject experts during validation evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A live-updating leaderboard is maintained at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard, with version changes tracked via a version change log.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Evaluates progress toward Expert AGI (Level 3 AGI), which marks a critical milestone denoting an AI system reaching at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults in broad tasks, thus beginning to achieve the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor, carrying significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI should tackle. Manual curation may carry biases, and focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for fully testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal foundation models, large language models (LLMs), and large multimodal models (LMMs) on multi-discipline multimodal understanding and deliberate reasoning. Divided into a few-shot development set (150 questions), validation set (900 questions for hyperparameter selection), and test set (10,500 questions).
